blocks.prompt: 8. Use binomial theorem to show that \(1 + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 8} + \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 8 \cdot 12} + \dots = \sqrt{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Left side ek la-mehdood series hai jis ki shakal binomial jaisi hai: upar odd numbers ke products, neeche \(4 \cdot 8 \cdot 12\).
Dikhana kya hai? Ke is ka jama \(\sqrt{2}\) hai.
Rule kaunsa? Series ko \((1 + x)^{n}\) maan kar \(n\) aur \(x\) dhoondna.
Plan: Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 8} + \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 8 \cdot 12} + \dots\)
Dikhana hai: jama \(\sqrt{2}\) hai.
Tareeqa: Farz karein yeh \((1 + x)^{n} = 1 + nx + \frac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots\) hai. Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge. Do namaloom cheezon ke liye do equations kaafi hain.

Do equations
\[nx = \dfrac{1}{4} \quad (1)\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2}x^{2} = \dfrac{3}{32} \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Doosri term \(\tfrac{1}{4}\) ko \(nx\) ke barabar rakha, aur teesri term \(\tfrac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 8} = \tfrac{3}{32}\) ko \(\tfrac{n(n - 1)}{2}x^{2}\) ke barabar.

\(n\) nikalein
\[n(n - 1)x^{2} = \dfrac{3}{16}\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)x^{2}}{(nx)^{2}} = \dfrac{3/16}{1/16} = 3\]
\[\dfrac{n - 1}{n} = 3 \Rightarrow n = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: (2) ko 2 se multiply kiya. Phir (1) ka square \((nx)^{2} = \tfrac{1}{16}\) se divide kiya: \(x^{2}\) aur ek \(n\) cancel ho gaye, sirf \(\tfrac{n - 1}{n}\) bacha. \(n - 1 = 3n\) se \(-1 = 2n\), yani \(n = -\tfrac{1}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: yeh divide karne wali chaal har aise sawal mein kaam aati hai; is se ek equation mein sirf \(n\) reh jata hai.

\(x\) nikalein
\[x = \dfrac{1/4}{n} = \dfrac{1/4}{-1/2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(n\) rakha. Negative \(n\) se divide kiya to \(x\) bhi negative aaya; is ka matlab bracket \(1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\) hai.

Chauthi term se tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})(-\frac{5}{2})}{3!}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{-15/8}{6} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{8}\right) = \dfrac{5}{128}\]
\[\dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 8 \cdot 12} = \dfrac{15}{384} = \dfrac{5}{128}\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Do terms se \(n\) aur \(x\) nikale the; teesri (yani chauthi term) bhi mil gayi, to pakka ho gaya ke pehchaan sahi hai.

Jama
\[\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-1/2}\]
\[= 2^{1/2} = \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(|x| = \tfrac{1}{2} < 1\) hai, is liye series converge karti hai. Negative power ne \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) ko ulta kar ke 2 bana diya, aur power \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) yani square root.
blocks.final_answer: Yeh \(\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right)^{-1/2}\) ki expansion hai, is liye \(1 + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 8} + \dots = \sqrt{2}\). Saabit ho gaya.
